title: P0 hosted API - signal amplification sleuth
content:
Summary:

Short summary: On 2028-11-30 02:15 UTC we observed a multi-region hosted-API degradation that surfaced as rising p95/p99 latency and an increase in streaming client 502/503 errors across US-WEST and EU-WEST. Impact window lasted ~47 minutes with partial recovery after an emergency autoscaler policy rollback and temporary disabling of adaptive batching. Customers experienced stalled streaming sessions and longer TTFB for non-streaming generation requests. This was declared P0 at 02:26 UTC.

Impact:
- High p95/p99 latency for generation endpoints (p99 increased from ~320ms to ~4.2s)
- Streaming clients receiving intermittent 502/503 and stream-halting behavior
- 0.8% increase in token cost due to retried requests and reduced batching efficiency during window
- Several enterprise customers reported degraded interactive latency (CS tickets opened)

How we detected it:
- Auto-alert: p99-latency-on-hostedapi > 1s for three consecutive 5m windows triggered SRE runbook pager at 02:22 UTC
- Multiple oncall Slack reports from solutions-engineering and a few inbound CS emails
- Dashboard time-series showed median stable but tail drifting; streaming error rate spiked first visible at 02:13 UTC in edge-telemetry

What we saw in telemetry (quick notes):
- Streaming-ack-latency histogram showed a rising mass at 300-600ms preceding token generation latency spike
- Multiplexer queue lengths increased on certain edge nodes; concurrent-kv-cache evictions observed for hot prefixes
- Autoscaler scaled up in two waves starting 02:18 and 02:23 but did not reduce tail until policy rollback
- Adaptive batching telemetry showed aggressive down-sizing of target batch sizes due to perceived increased per-request latency (feedback loop)

Immediate mitigation timeline (actions taken):
- 02:24 UTC: SRE runbook invoked; initial triage + ownership assigned to SRE response lead (Aisha)
- 02:27 UTC: Disabled adaptive-batching flag globally for hosted-api to break feedback loop (quick rollback of feature flag)
- 02:30 UTC: Temporarily pinned streaming clients to stable model variant (smaller KV working set) for several customers while we stabilized
- 02:34 UTC: Rolled back the recent autoscaler policy change that had shortened cooldown and increased aggressiveness (policy from PR #2130)
- 02:45 UTC: Observed p99 drop to ~700-900ms; streaming error rates began to normalize
- 03:02 UTC: Service declared recovered; continued monitoring for 2 hours

Root cause (current working hypothesis):
This incident was caused by a multi-factor feedback amplification loop between: 1) adaptive batching heuristics reacting to increased per-request processing times, 2) an autoscaler policy change that responded too aggressively to transient latency signals, and 3) a shard-local KV cache churn caused by a tokenizer-induced prefix hotness shift. Sequence: tokenizer change in last model rollout produced slightly different tokenization distributions for some common prefixes. That increased KV cache churn for a subset of shards which temporarily increased per-token latency for requests routed to those shards. Adaptive-batching observed higher per-request latency and assumed smaller batches would restore latency, reducing batching efficiency and increasing per-token cost. Meanwhile, autoscaler policy interpreted the tail latency as an under-provisioning signal and rapidly added capacity, which caused rebalancing and cold-KV hits across nodes, further amplifying KV churn. The combined effect led to sustained p95/p99 elevation and intermittent streaming 502/503s as multiplexer queues hit headroom and connection timeouts were hit.

Evidence supporting hypothesis:
- Correlation between tokenizer rollout time (23:58 previous night) and first telemetry uptick in KV eviction rate for certain prefixes
- Logs show increased KV miss latency on a small set of shards, with median per-token generation time rising by ~35% on those shards
- Adaptive-batching logs: multiple back-to-back downward batch_size adjustments starting exactly when per-request latency rose, with reduced batch occupancy across the fleet
- Autoscaler timeline: aggressive policy change merged 2028-11-28 increased scaling aggressiveness; timestamps show scale-up events coincident with rising latency
- Reproduced locally: running a small synthetic workload with the new tokenizer and current KV config triggers higher eviction and misses on single-shard configs

What didn't cause it (ruled out):
- No evidence of network-wide connectivity events or cloud provider maintenance during window
- No recent TLS/edge infra changes in the window (checked edge changelog and deployment timeline)
- No storage tier failures (S3/Blobstore metrics normal)

What we tried (failed or partial):
- Increasing per-node memory limits briefly reduced eviction rate but did not stop amplification once autoscaler and adaptive-batching were both active
- Rate-limiting specific prefixes at the edge reduced tail for those prefixes but created customer-facing retries—unacceptable as an emergency mitigation

Short-term mitigations (post-incident actions that remain in place):
- Keep adaptive-batching disabled by default until we push safer heuristics (feature flag guarded)
- Revert autoscaler policy to conservative settings and add a staged rollout to avoid global rapid scale actions
- Pin model tokenizer variant for hosted-api until we complete extended canary and KV heatmap tests

Longer-term remediation plan (owners and ETA rough):
1) Improve adaptive-batching heuristics to be shard-aware and avoid reacting to localized cache churn (owner: Diego, ETA: 4 weeks)
2) Add a KV-cache telemetry heatmap that maps prefixes to shard eviction/miss rates and surfaces when tokenization changes alter heat (owner: Sara, ETA: 3 weeks)
3) Autoscaler policy change: introduce signal smoothing and cluster-level hysteresis; require canary rollout gating for policy changes (owner: Omar, ETA: 2 weeks)
4) Model rollout process change: enforce KV-heatmap smoke test in the deployment CI that simulates token distribution shifts before global rollout (owner: Product infra, ETA: 3 weeks)
5) Backpressure runbook update: add specific steps to pause adaptive-batching and to pin routing to unaffected shards when eviction spikes detected (owner: Evan, ETA: 1 week)
6) Follow-up: run postmortem blameless review with product, serving-runtime, and SRE (owner: Aisha, meeting target 2028-12-05)

Runbook draft (emergency steps to break this class of amplification loops):
- Pager fires for p99 > 1s for 3 windows or streaming error rate > 0.5%
- Triage: identify whether KV eviction rate increased on any shards (dashboards: kv-eviction-by-shard, multiplexer-queue-length)
- If eviction spike present: disable adaptive-batching globally (feature flag) and pin clients to previous model tokenizer variant
- If autoscaler activity is contributing (scale ups within last 10m): revert to conservative policy and pause automatic scaling for 10m for the affected region
- If multiplexer queue headroom < 15%: increase per-edge queue headroom (soft config) OR move selected traffic away to healthy edges
- Notify customer-facing teams with templated message (CS/Sales) about degraded interactive latency and mitigation steps

Open action items (immediate):
- [Aisha] Draft external customer note template and coordinate with CS (due 2028-12-01)
- [Diego] Start design doc for shard-aware adaptive-batching (due 2028-12-14)
- [Sara] Implement KV heatmap prototype (POC data in next 2 weeks)
- [Omar] Rework autoscaler PR to add staged rollout and smoothing (PR expected 1 week)
- [Evan] Update SRE runbook page with the new emergency steps and run tabletop exercise (due 2028-12-08)

Notes and questions to investigate further:
- How much did specific tokenizer token boundary changes contribute? Need diff against previous tokenizer output for top-1000 prefixes
- Could we introduce a soft local-batch-hold to avoid batch-size oscillation when per-request latency variance is high?
- Investigate whether routing policy can preferentially route sensitive low-latency customers away from shards with recent eviction spikes

Appendix (observability pointers and commands):
- Dashboards: hostedapi/p99-latency, streaming/errors-by-edge, kv/evictions-by-shard, batching/occupancy-by-region
- Useful logs: serving-runtime multiplexer trace: trace_id prefixed with mpx-; kv-agent debug logs at INFO+ for shardId X
- Quick queries:
  - Count of eviction events: "sum(rate(kv_evictions_total[1m])) by (shard)"
  - Batch occupancy: "histogram_quantile(0.9, sum(rate(batch_occupancy_bucket[1m])) by (le, region))"

Slack/war-room notes (copied fragments):
- 02:19 SRE: "seeing p99 go up on a couple edges, kv eviction climb correlates, canary tokenizer rolled last night?"
- 02:28 Diego: "disabled adaptive-batching, immediately saw reduction in batch oscillation"
- 02:33 Omar: "reverted autoscaler policy from PR #2130, cold hit pattern stabilizing"

Final note: Blameless postmortem coming; primary goal is to close the feedback loop between infra heuristics (autoscaler, batching) and workload-level signals (tokenization, kv churn). We were saved by quick runbook steps but need engineering changes to avoid recurrence.
